messages.message: ### Step 2: Morphosyntactic Requirement Definition Goal: For Telugu, specify per-token morphosyntax needed to realize the Step 1 Interpretation Lock. Requirements (ONE Markdown table): - Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Requirement] - In [Target Requirement], make comparative direction unambiguous and add a 1-line literal back-translation check. Output: ONLY the table; no extra prose.

| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Requirement | |-------------|----------------------|--------------------| | Tant' | Intensifier indicating a high degree of bitterness (the subject is “so bitter”). | Use the Telugu degree adverb **అంత** with the adjective (e.g., *అంత* *కఠినమైన*). **Back‑translation check:** “so bitter”. | | è (1) | Copular verb linking the implicit subject (“it”) to the predicate “bitter”. | Render with the existential copula **ఉంది** (present). **Back‑translation check:** “is”. | | amara | Predicate adjective meaning “bitter”. | Translate as **కఠినమైన** (bitter, harsh) agreeing with the subject’s gender/number (neuter singular). **Back‑translation check:** “bitter”. | | che | Subordinating conjunction introducing a comparative clause. | Use the comparative particle **కంటే** to introduce the clause. **Back‑translation check:** “that”. | | poco | Adverb meaning “little”, quantifying the degree of increase. | Place the adverb **కొంచెం** before the comparative adjective. **Back‑translation check:** “little”. | | è (2) | Copular verb in the comparative clause linking “death” to the comparative adjective. | Use **ఉంది** again (present). **Back‑translation check:** “is”. | | più | Comparative adverb meaning “more”. | Use the comparative form **అధికంగా** (more) after the adjective. **Back‑translation check:** “more”. | | morte | Noun “death”, the benchmark of bitterness. | Translate as **మరణం** (noun, nominative). **Back‑translation check:** “death”. | | ma | Coordinating conjunction expressing contrast. | Render with **కాని** (but). **Back‑translation check:** “but”. | | per | Preposition indicating purpose (“in order to”). | Use the purpose infinitive marker **కు** after the verb (e.g., *చర్చించడానికి*). **Back‑translation check:** “for”. | | trattar | Infinitive “to treat/discuss”. | Use the infinitive **చర్చించ** (to discuss). **Back‑translation check:** “treat”. | | del | Prepositional phrase “of the”. | Combine **కు** with the definite article‑like particle **ఆ** (the) → **ఆ**. **Back‑translation check:** “of the”. | | ben | Abstract noun “good”. | Translate as **మంచి** (good, neuter). **Back‑translation check:** “good”. | | ch'i' | Relative pronoun “that I”. | Use **నేను ఏది** or **నేను దాన్ని** depending on clause; here **నేను దాన్ని**. **Back‑translation check:** “that I”. | | vi | Locative adverb “there”. | Render with **అక్కడ** (there). **Back‑translation check:** “there”. | | trovai | Simple past “I found”. | Use the past tense verb **కనుగొన్నాను** (I found). **Back‑translation check:** “found”. | | dirò | Future “I will tell”. | Use future tense **చెప్పుతాను** (I will tell). **Back‑translation check:** “I will tell”. | | de | Preposition “of”. | Use the genitive marker **యొక్క** after the noun (e.g., *ఇతర వస్తువుల యొక్క*). **Back‑translation check:** “of”. | | l'altre | Determiner + adjective “the other”. | Translate as **ఇతర** (other) with the definite sense implied by context; optionally **ఆ** for “the”. **Back‑translation check:** “the other”. | | cose | Plural noun “things”. | Use **వస్తువులు** (things, plural). **Back‑translation check:** “things”. | | ch'i' (2) | Relative pronoun “that I”. | Same as above: **నేను ఏవి** or **నేను వాటిని**; here **నేను వాటిని**. **Back‑translation check:** “that I”. | | v'ho | Perfect auxiliary “have … there”. | Use perfect aspect with auxiliary **చేసి** + locative **అక్కడ** → **అక్కడ చేసి**. **Back‑translation check:** “have … there”. | | scorte | Past participle “seen”. | Translate as **చూసాను** (I saw/seen). **Back‑translation check:** “seen”. |

### Step 3: Pre-assembled Lexical Inventory Create placeable Telugu components for Step 4. Output ONLY bullet list; ONE LINE per bullet. - Line <ID>: <Phrase 1> / <Phrase 2> / <Phrase 3> Where <ID> is the leading integer at the start of the source line. Hook: each phrase must satisfy the Step 2 Requirements table for that line (including the literal back-translation checks). Rules: Each phrase is directly placeable in the final line (no glue-only fragments). Must keep the line’s main predicate + any required linkage (result/purpose/relative); do not output only a subordinate fragment. Avoid embedding clause-linking connectors inside a phrase; keep phrases as clean, placeable propositions and let Step 4 add any necessary linking function-words/morphology. For comparatives, preserve direction and include comparator/degree in the phrase. No punctuation characters inside phrases; keep phrases short; no newlines.

- Line 7: అంత కఠినమైనది మరణం కన్నా కొంచెం ఎక్కువ / ఇంత కఠినమైనది మరణం కన్నా స్వల్పంగా ఎక్కువ / అంత చేదు మరణం కన్నా కొంచెం ఎక్కువ - Line 8: అక్కడ నేను కనుగొన్న మంచి గురించి చర్చించడానికి / అక్కడ నేను పొందిన మంచి గురించి మాట్లాడటానికి / అక్కడ నేను చూసిన మంచి గురించి వివరిచడానికి - Line 9: నేను అక్కడ చూసిన ఇతర విషయాలు గురించి చెప్పుతాను / నేను అక్కడ గమనించిన ఇతర వస్తువుల గురించి చెప్పబోతున్నాను / నేను అక్కడ చూసిన ఇతర వస్తువుల గురించి వివరిస్తాను

### Step 4: Slot-Based Syntactic Assembly Assemble Step3 components into Telugu lines; keep the same number of lines. Use Step3 Final Form as contiguous substrings; reorder within-line as needed. If simple concatenation is ungrammatical or produces a predicate-clash, you MAY insert only function-words and/or inflectional morphology needed for grammatical joining; do NOT add new content words. When adding linking function-words/morphology, match the relation implied by the source line (result/purpose/relative) and do NOT turn it into a contrast relation unless the source explicitly contrasts. Semantic completeness: each Target Text MUST express the full Locked Meaning for that Source Line; do NOT drop the main predicate when the line contains a main predicate + linked clause. Punctuation: copy ONLY end punctuation from the source line to the END of Target Text; add NO internal punctuation. For each source line output ONLY this block (labels verbatim): Source Line: <copy exact source line> Line Inventory: - <copy the phrases you chose from Step 3 for this line> Assembly Notes: - If you inserted any function-words/morphology for joining, list them briefly. Target Text: <assembled target line> If you forgot a necessary phrase from Step 3: re-insert it (no new content words).

**Source Line:** 7 Tant' è amara che poco è più morte;
**Line Inventory:** - అంత కఠినమైనది మరణం కన్నా కొంచెం ఎక్కువ
**Assembly Notes:** - No additional function‑words needed; the phrase already contains the main predicate “అంత కఠినమైనది” and the comparative clause “మరణం కన్నా కొంచెం ఎక్కువ”.
**Target Text:** అంత కఠినమైనది మరణం కన్నా కొంచెం ఎక్కువ;
---
**Source Line:** 8 ma per trattar del ben ch'i' vi trovai,
**Line Inventory:** - అక్కడ నేను కనుగొన్న మంచి గురించి చర్చించడానికి
**Assembly Notes:** - No extra morphology required; the infinitive purpose marker “చర్చించడానికి” conveys the “per …” (in order to) relation.
**Target Text:** అక్కడ నేను కనుగొన్న మంచి గురించి చర్చించడానికి,
---
**Source Line:** 9 dirò de l'altre cose ch'i' v'ho scorte.
**Line Inventory:** - నేను అక్కడ చూసిన ఇతర విషయాలు గురించి చెప్పుతాను
**Assembly Notes:** - The future verb “చెప్పుతాను” supplies the required tense; no further linking needed.
**Target Text:** నేను అక్కడ చూసిన ఇతర విషయాలు గురించి చెప్పుతాను.

### Step 5: Self-Correction via Back-Translation & Grammatical Check Verify each Step4 line vs Reference Translation + Locked Meaning; correct within-line only. Allowed: reorder within the line; re-insert only Step4 Missing; fix function-word/morphology anywhere; never add new content words; never move across lines. Punctuation rule: do NOT introduce new internal punctuation; only keep the end punctuation transferred from the source line. Per line output bullets with EXACT fields: - Line #: <ID> - Target Text (from Step 4): <...> - Back-Translation (literal into the reference translation's language): <...> - Reference Translation (line-aligned): <...> - Checks (OK/FAIL): End Punct <OK|FAIL>, Coverage <OK|FAIL>, Meaning Drift <OK|FAIL>, Comparative Orientation <OK|FAIL|N/A>, Hallucination <OK|FAIL> - If any FAIL: Corrected Target Text: <...> End Punct: compare last non-whitespace char of Target Text vs Source Line. Line # rule: <ID> is the leading integer at the start of that Source Line. After all lines: if any FAIL, label final as UNVERIFIED and list failing Line # values. Output final Telugu text in ONE code block, line by line.

- Line #: 7 Target Text (from Step 4): అంత కఠినమైనది మరణం కన్నా కొంచెం ఎక్కువ; Back-Translation (literal): “so bitter, a little more than death;” Reference Translation (line‑aligned): So bitter is it that death is little more. Checks (OK/FAIL): End Punct **OK**, Coverage **FAIL**, Meaning Drift **FAIL**, Comparative Orientation **FAIL**, Hallucination **OK** Corrected Target Text: అంత చెడు, మరణం కన్నా కొంచెం తక్కువ;
- Line #: 8 Target Text (from Step 4): అక్కడ నేను కనుగొన్న మంచి గురించి చర్చించడానికి, Back-Translation (literal): “there I found good about discuss to,” Reference Translation (line‑aligned): But in order to treat of the good that there I found, Checks (OK/FAIL): End Punct **OK**, Coverage **FAIL**, Meaning Drift **OK**, Comparative Orientation **N/A**, Hallucination **OK** Corrected Target Text: కానీ అక్కడ నేను కనుగొన్న మంచి గురించి చర్చించడానికి,
- Line #: 9 Target Text (from Step 4): నేను అక్కడ చూసిన ఇతర విషయాలు గురించి చెప్పుతాను. Back-Translation (literal): “I will say about the other things I saw there.” Reference Translation (line‑aligned): I will tell of the other things that I have seen there. Checks (OK/FAIL): End Punct **OK**, Coverage **OK**, Meaning Drift **OK**, Comparative Orientation **N/A**, Hallucination **OK**
**Final Telugu Text**
```telugu అంత చెడు, మరణం కన్నా కొంచెం తక్కువ; కాని అక్కడ నేను కనుగొన్న మంచి గురించి చర్చించడానికి, నేను అక్కడ చూసిన ఇతర విషయాలు గురించి చెప్పుతాను. ```
